To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
platinum chemotherapy and cranial radiation therapy are the most important risk factors for HL in childhood cancer survivors.
platinum‐based chemotherapy and/or craniospinal radiotherapy increase the risk of hearing loss in children and adolescents treated for cancer.

(1) platinum‐based chemotherapy and/or craniospinal radiation are associated with increased risk for hearing loss (HL) in survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer, (2) HL in childhood cancer survivors is underdiagnosed and undertreated, (3) HL can have a significant impact on the quality of life of survivors, and (4) HL in childhood and adolescent cancer survivors is treatable.

the evaluation and management of hearing loss in childhood cancer survivors.

hearing loss is common among childhood cancer survivors and can be mitigated through early detection and intervention.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HL is common in childhood and adolescent cancer survivors, especially in those exposed to platinum chemotherapy or cranial radiation.
the Children’s Oncology Group Hearing Loss Task Force has developed a set of guidelines for the evaluation and management of hearing loss in survivors of childhood cancer.

the Children's Oncologic Group (COG) has been working on a multi‐center, prospective, longitudinal study to evaluate the incidence, risk factors, and impact of HL on the quality of life of pediatric cancer survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HL is common among childhood cancer survivors, and survivors and providers should be vigilant about early detection of HL.

early identification of survivors with HL is important to mitigate academic, speech/language, and social/psychological morbidity resulting from HL and that early referral to an audiologic provider is important to identify the etiology of HL.
HL is a common and potentially devastating late effect of treatment for childhood and adolescent cancers and that appropriate management can mitigate the impact of HL on quality of life.
